The following morning, Professor Stone is again at the desk beneath the library’s iron stair. He is sorting borrowing slips into narrow wooden trays when you approach.

“Which publicly available records describe the human seat’s last active years?” you ask. “I’d like to look at the original records if they’re open to students.”

Stone’s hand remains on one slip for a moment. His eyes move toward the locked glass cabinet at the rear of the library.

“Original and publicly available are separate categories here.”

He leaves the desk and leads you to the history shelves.

“The last active holder was Councilor Dan Garvey. For his final decade, the open collection has three useful sources.”

He removes a thick grey volume titled *The Human Delegation in Its Final Years*, followed by several bound annual summaries and an indexed set of Council abstracts.

“The retrospective was compiled after the seat became vacant. The annual volumes summarize the Concordance Office’s arbitrations, expenditures, and formal recommendations. The Council abstracts record motions, votes, and outcomes.”

Stone places them on a reading table.

“Do not mistake the abstracts for transcripts. They omit most debate and identify private sessions only by date and subject.”

The original material, he explains, includes complete Council minutes, petitions, correspondence from Garvey’s office, and unabridged arbitration files. All primary records from the period are held under restricted access. Conclave students may request supervised use, but each request requires a specific catalog reference, a faculty sponsor, and Chancellor Ashworth’s signature.

“The restriction order cites fragile documents, private correspondence, and agreements whose obligations may still be active,” Stone says. “A request for everything from the final years will be denied as too broad. Use the green finding index first. It will tell you which files exist, though not always what they contain.”

He adds the index to the stack. Its public headings divide the last years of the human seat into Council votes, treaty review, arbitration, internal administration, and emergency measures during the first plague year.

Stone returns to his desk without offering access beyond the official process.

The public summaries and the finding index remain open to you. Across the room, the original records sit behind locked glass.
reasoning_summaries: **Listing public record types with guarded details**
**Defining timeline and access limits for records**
